expectations.text: Module has a docstring with a one-line summary of what the module provides
expectations.evidence: First line: "Token-bucket rate limiter." followed by expanded description.

expectations.text: TokenBucket class docstring includes an Attributes: section documenting public attributes
expectations.evidence: Class docstring lines 51-53: "Attributes:" documenting rate and capacity, which are the public attributes (self.rate, self.capacity).

expectations.text: acquire and try_acquire have docstrings with Args: and Returns: sections; Raises: present where the code raises for invalid input
expectations.evidence: Both have Args:, Returns:, Raises: ("ValueError: If ``n`` is not positive, exceeds ``capacity``, or if ``timeout`` is negative."), matching the actual raises.

expectations.text: All docstrings use triple double quotes with descriptive (not imperative) first lines ending in a period
expectations.evidence: All 8 docstrings use """; first lines descriptive with periods, e.g. "Acquires ``n`` tokens, blocking until they are available.", "Validates a token request size.", "Adds tokens accrued since the last refill."

expectations.text: With type annotations present, docstrings describe semantics without repeating the types
expectations.evidence: Annotated params are described semantically ("timeout: Maximum number of seconds to wait."); the only type mention ("callable returning ... a float") is for the unannotated clock parameter.

expectations.text: try_acquire's Returns: explains the True/False semantics; acquire documents its blocking behavior
expectations.evidence: try_acquire Returns: "True if the tokens were available and have been consumed, False if there were not enough tokens..."; acquire: "blocking until they are available" and "this method sleeps until enough tokens have been refilled".

expectations.text: Any inline comments are separated from code by at least two spaces and explain intent rather than restating code
expectations.evidence: One trailing comment, line 91: "self._tokens = self.capacity  # Bucket starts full." — two spaces, states the invariant/intent; block comments (lines 147, 155-156) also explain intent.

expectations.text: Thread-safety behavior is stated in the class or module docstring (either safe or not — just stated)
expectations.evidence: Class docstring: "A thread-safe token-bucket rate limiter." plus a dedicated "Thread safety:" paragraph (lines 55-59).

summary.notes: Thorough documentation that happens to satisfy all shared assertions, though it mixes in reST markup (``x``, :meth:) rather than pure Google style.
